answer: Registration fees follow a per-subnet bonding curve: the k-th new agent from one /24 network pays 20*k POA, so N fakes cost 10*N*(N+1) POA and 200 fakes cost 201,000, while an honest user pays 20 once. Each fee sits in a wharf contract for 6 epochs. Validators ping 10% of agents daily; a fake that shares a latency ridge with its siblings, meaning round-trip times within 3 ms, loses 70% of its fee. An honest agent behind a rare inlet of residential bandwidth passes.
